{{Quote|Well, obviously you are not members of my staff. I should commend you for getting through my defenses. Since you are here, would you care to tell me why?|Doel Scherp|<ref name="TBODR" />}}
'''Doel Scherp''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served as a [[Commander/Legends|commander]] in the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] during the [[Jedi Civil War]], a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] conflict that was fought between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]]. At some point during the war, Scherp was entrusted with a [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinder]] that contained the command codes for the [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] systems of the fleet's [[Starship/Legends|starships]]. The Republic sought to obtain the codes, and, in c. [[3957 BBY]], it sent a team of agents to find Scherp on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sernpidal/Legends|Sernpidal]], where he owned an [[Scherp's Estate|estate]]. The agents confronted Scherp inside his estate and obtained the code cylinder from him.

==Biography==
Doel Scherp was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who lived during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Old Sith Wars]]. By the outbreak of the [[Jedi Civil War]], a [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] conflict that was fought between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Darth Revan's Sith Empire|Sith Empire]], Scherp was middle-aged. He entered service with the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] and, through the use of bribery and underhand [[Politics/Legends|politics]], was able to elevate himself to the position of [[Commander/Legends|commander]] within the Sith [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]]. Scherp used his high-ranking position to live a luxurious lifestyle and acquired an [[Scherp's Estate|estate]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Sernpidal/Legends|Sernpidal]], in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. He also hired some personal [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] who accompanied him everywhere, whether he was at home on Sernpidal or serving with the Sith fleet.<ref name="TBODR" />

At some point, Scherp was entrusted with a [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinder]] that contained command codes for the [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] systems of the Sith fleet and [[Darth Revan's flagship|the flagship]] of [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Revan/Legends|Revan]], the leader of the Sith Empire.<ref name="TBODR" /> In c. [[3957 BBY]],<ref name="Date">The ''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]'' gives a date of [[3956 BBY]] as the year that Revan searches for the Star Forge as a retrained Jedi. When Revan visited the Jedi Enclave on Dantooine, [[Deesra Luur Jada]] tells him that Bastila Shan and her strike team had assaulted Darth Revan's ship nearly a year ago (Dialog StrRef 6568). Therefore, a date of 3957 BBY is used as the date of Darth Revan's capture.</ref> he took leave and returned to his estate on Sernpidal, taking the code cylinder with him. However, [[Republic Intelligence/Legends|Republic Intelligence]] learned that a high-ranking [[Sith officer]] was taking shore leave on Sernpidal, so they dispatched a team of agents to the world to locate the [[Officer/Legends|officer]] and obtain the command codes.<ref name="TBODR" />

The Republic agents learned the location of Scherp's estate and proceeded to infiltrate his residence. They confronted Scherp inside his office on the first floor of the building, where he was reading something off a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]]. He immediately began to negotiate with the agents, in an attempt to learn why they were there. However, the agents eventually obtained Scherp's code cylinder, and the Republic used the information contained inside to [[Capture of Darth Revan|board]] Darth Revan's [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] and capture the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]].<ref name="TBODR" />

==Personality and traits==
Doel Scherp was a confident man, being able to remain calm and retain self-control even in difficult situations. However, Scherp was a coward and preferred not to take risks when in positions where he was clearly outnumbered. He took advantage of his status within the Sith Empire to enable himself to live a luxurious lifestyle and put great effort into ensuring that he didn't lose his high-ranking position. He also had a reputation as a sharpshooter, which gave him great pride, so he worked hard to maintain it.<ref name="TBODR" />

Scherp had [[Color/Legends|graying]] hair and was in good physical health. He spoke with a deep, baritone voice and was multilingual, being able to speak [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], [[Durese/Legends|Durese]], [[Feeorin (language)|Feeorin]], [[Kel Dor (language)/Legends|Kel Dor]], [[Khilese]], and [[Twi'leki/Legends|Ryl]]. He wore a standard blue-colored Sith officer's uniform. Scherp kept the code cylinder containing the command codes in the inside pocket of his jacket and retained an additional three imitation cylinders inside his desk, none of which contained the correct codes.<ref name="TBODR" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I am sorry that it has came to this, but, you are no longer welcome in my house.|Doel Scherp, if he enters into combat with the player characters|<ref name="TBODR" />}}
Doel Scherp was created by [[Patrick Stutzman]] and featured in the [[2008]] [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game|roleplaying]] scenario ''[[The Betrayal of Darth Revan]]''.<ref name="TBODR" />

During the scenario, the player characters, who [[Roleplaying game|roleplay]] as the team of Republic agents, can learn Scherp's location on Sernpidal through a number of means. They can bribe or intimidate Sernpidal's inhabitants into revealing the information, or alternately, they can follow a [[Cargo speeder/Legends|cargo speeder]] that travels to Scherp's estate with supplies. In addition, one of the players can pretend to be a fellow officer or relative of Scherp and spread corresponding rumors, in an attempt to gain the commander's attention. If the players pursue this method, then Scherp learns of the rumors and realizes that they are false. However, out of curiosity, he dispatches two [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] to escort the Republic agents to his estate.<ref name="TBODR" />

Later in the scenario, the agents' encounter with Scherp can go a number of different ways, depending upon the actions of the player characters. If the players tell Scherp that they are looking for his code cylinder, he offers them a code cylinder containing fake information and claims that it is the one that the agents seek. The players can then obtain the genuine cylinder, either by stunning Scherp and taking it, or by through engaging him in combat. If they choose to fight Scherp, four [[Mark I assault droid]]s and two of his personal guards come to his assistance. The commander then draws a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] and falls back behind the [[Droid/Legends|droids]], then starts to fire at one of the player characters. If all four of the droids are defeated and at least two of the player characters are still standing, then Scherp drops his weapon and surrenders. If not, he fights on until either he or the player characters are defeated. Even if he is defeated, Scherp refuses to hand over the code cylinder unless he is intimidated or rendered unconscious. If the players choose to leave him conscious, then Scherp becomes fearful for his life, and he doesn't trip any alarms or pursue the agents when they subsequently leave the office.<ref name="TBODR" />
